questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the "elasticity" feature of cloud computing?

options.text: The ability to deploy resources to multiple geographic regions simultaneously.
The ability to automatically scale resources up and down based on demand.
The ability to pay only for resources you actually consume.
The ability to recover from service outages without data loss.

questions.explanation: Elasticity specifically refers to the dynamic allocation and deallocation of resources to match demand. Option C describes the consumption-based pricing model. Option A describes geographic redundancy. Option D describes resilience and disaster recovery.

questions.stem: A company wants to retain full control over the operating system, network configuration, and storage of their workload, while delegating only the physical hardware management to Microsoft. Which cloud service model meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: IaaS provides virtual machines where the customer manages the OS, networking, and storage; Microsoft manages only the physical hardware. PaaS abstracts the OS layer. SaaS delivers a complete application. FaaS abstracts both the OS and the application server.

questions.stem: Which type of cloud deployment combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources, allowing data and applications to move between them?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud explicitly combines on-premises (private) and public cloud resources with orchestrated workload mobility between them. Public cloud uses only third-party infrastructure. Private cloud is entirely on-premises or single-tenant. Community cloud is shared among related organizations.

questions.stem: A team needs to run small, event-driven code without provisioning or managing servers, paying only when the code executes. Which Azure service best fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service that runs code on triggers and bills per execution. VMs require server management. App Service hosts persistent web apps with always-on pricing. AKS requires cluster management.

questions.stem: Which Azure storage service is best suited for storing massive amounts of unstructured data such as images, documents, and backups?
questions.explanation: Blob Storage is designed for unstructured data at massive scale (text, binary, media). Azure Files provides SMB/NFS file shares. Disk Storage is for VM disks. Table Storage is for structured NoSQL key-value data.

questions.stem: Two Azure regions are paired together to provide redundancy and protection against regional outages. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Region pairs are pre-defined pairings within the same geography that provide cross-region replication for redundancy. Availability zones are within a single region. Resource groups are logical containers. Geographies are the broader top-level grouping.

questions.stem: Which Azure service helps you analyze a workload's actual cost, identify spending anomalies, and forecast future spend?
questions.explanation: Azure Cost Management is the dedicated service for cost analysis, budgets, and forecasting. Advisor gives recommendations across cost, security, and performance — not in-depth cost analysis. Policy enforces compliance rules. Monitor tracks performance and availability metrics.

questions.stem: You need to enforce that all storage accounts in a subscription must use HTTPS-only traffic. Which service should you use?
questions.explanation: Azure Policy enforces resource configuration standards through definitions and assignments — exactly the use case described. Blueprints bundle environments. Defender provides security recommendations and threat protection but does not enforce configuration rules. RBAC controls who can perform actions, not what configurations resources must have.

questions.stem: Your organization's billing department needs read-only access to view costs across all subscriptions but should not be able to modify any resources. What is the most appropriate Azure feature to grant this access?

options.text: Assigning the "Owner" role at the management group level.
Assigning the built-in "Billing Reader" RBAC role at the appropriate scope.
Sharing the global administrator account credentials.
Creating a custom Azure AD group with no permissions.

questions.explanation: Built-in RBAC roles like Billing Reader are designed for least-privilege scenarios — read-only billing and cost access. Owner grants full access including resource modification. Sharing credentials violates security best practices. A group with no permissions would not grant the needed access.

questions.stem: Which Azure support plan is required to receive 24/7 phone support for a production workload?
questions.explanation: The Standard support plan and above include 24/7 phone support for production workloads. Basic and Free include only billing and subscription support. Developer supports business-hours email/web for non-production environments.
